title: Election calendar, October 2026 to December 2027
coverage: Lok Sabha and assembly bypolls, Rajya Sabha elections, state assembly general elections and the presidential election, plus major state election commission rural local body polls, held, announced or expected between 1 October 2026 and 31 December 2027. Only items confirmed in at least one reputable source are listed.

rows.name: Nagaon Lok Sabha bypoll
rows.result: Devasish Sharma (BJP) beat Badruddin Ajmal (AIUDF) by 1,42,224 votes (7,14,349 to 5,72,125). BJP gain from Congress.
rows.source_publisher: DD News, citing Election Commission figures
rows.notes: Vacancy caused by the resignation of Pradyut Bordoloi, elected on a Congress ticket in 2024, who joined the BJP and won the Dispur assembly seat in 2026 (DD News). Third place: Sibamoni Bora (Congress). Other reported margins: 1,40,257 (ETV Bharat live blog), 1,57,804 (IANS, from trends). Confirm on results.eci.gov.in.

rows.name: Nandigram assembly bypoll
rows.result: Hasirani Rath (BJP) beat Milan Pradhan (Congress) by 1,22,753 votes (1,64,427 to 41,674).
rows.notes: Seat vacated by Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, who kept Bhabanipur.

rows.name: Rejinagar assembly bypoll
rows.result: Shankharavh Sarkar (BJP) beat Golam Nabi Azad (AJUP) by 75,816 votes (1,29,914 to 54,098).
rows.notes: Seat vacated by Humayun Kabir, who kept Naoda. Winner's name spelt variously.

rows.name: Madurantakam (SC) assembly bypoll
rows.result: K. Maragatham Kumaravel (TVK) beat I. Paranthamen (DMK) by 20,081 votes (72,149 to 52,068).
rows.notes: ETV Bharat's live blog gave a margin of 19,312 at an earlier stage. Vacated when the AIADMK MLA resigned and joined TVK.

rows.name: Dharapuram (SC) assembly bypoll
rows.result: P. Sathyabama (TVK) beat S. Suganya (DMK) by 9,471 votes (66,841 to 57,370).
rows.notes: Vacated when the AIADMK MLA resigned and joined TVK.

rows.name: Thattanchavady assembly bypoll
rows.result: Ashok Anand (AINRC) beat E. Vinayagam (Congress) by 8,482 votes (13,358 to 4,876).
rows.source_publisher: The Pioneer, citing the Election Commission; margin matches ETV Bharat
rows.notes: Seat vacated by Chief Minister N. Rangasamy.

rows.name: Rajya Sabha biennial election, Uttar Pradesh
rows.result: All 10 elected unopposed, declared on 9 October: BJP 8 (Dharm Pal Singh, Prakash Pal, Shruti Gangwar, Vidyasagar Sonkar, Priyanka Singh Rawat, Radhakant Ojha, Gopi Krishna Pandey, Ram Pratap Singh Chauhan), SP 2 (Ram Gopal Yadav, Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani). Poll scheduled for 16 October not needed.
rows.notes: term_end is the retirement date of the outgoing members (News on AIR, 29 Sep 2026: https://newsonair.gov.in/ec-issues-notification-for-biennial-elections-to-11-rajya-sabha-seats/). 'date' is the date the result was declared.

rows.name: Rajya Sabha biennial election, Uttarakhand
rows.result: Dinesh Arya (BJP) elected unopposed on 9 October.
rows.notes: Seat held by BJP's Naresh Bansal, whose term expires on 25 November 2026. 'date' is the date the result was declared. Also confirmed by DD News, 9 Oct 2026.

rows.name: Rajya Sabha bypoll, West Bengal
rows.result: Rukmini (Koel) Mallick (BJP) elected unopposed, per IANS.
rows.notes: Result confirmed by IANS (Hans India) and DD News (9 Oct 2026, https://ddindia.co.in/2026/10/bjp-wins-eight-sp-two-of-ups-10-rajya-sabha-seats-unopposed/). Vacancy caused by Mallick's own resignation on 16 Jul 2026 as a TMC member (IANS). Poll had been scheduled for 16 October.

rows.name: Andhra Pradesh Mandal and Zilla Parishad (MPTC and ZPTC) elections
rows.result: Final, as released by the State Election Commission on the night of November 8, 2026 (10:55 pm IST): ZPTC (582 contested seats) NDA 499 (TDP 406, Jana Sena 73, BJP 20), YSRCP 76, CPI(M) 1, independents 6. MPTC (7,768 contested seats) NDA 5,861 (TDP 4,806, Jana Sena 938, BJP 117), YSRCP 1,711, CPI(M) 15, independents 162. Congress won none. The TDP-led alliance took about 86% of ZPTC and 75% of MPTC seats contested.
rows.source_publisher: Daijiworld, citing the State Election Commission's final results
rows.notes: Local body poll run by the Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission (not the ECI), listed because it is the largest rural vote of the period. seats = 7,767 MPTC + 582 ZPTC seats contested; a further 2,051 MPTC and 77 ZPTC seats were decided unopposed, and three MPTC seats have no valid candidate (SEC figures via The Hans India). Polling was moved from 3 Nov to 5 Nov (South First, https://thesouthfirst.com/andhrapradesh/ap-mptc-zptc-poll-schedule-revised-polling-on-5-november-counting-on-7-november/) and held from 7 am to 5 pm on 5 Nov, with about 2.61 crore voters. Because of heavy rain from Cyclone Murasu, the SEC put off polling in four Eluru district mandals (Buttaigudem, Jeelugumilli, Velerupadu and Polavaram) to Friday 6 Nov. SEC turnout for 5 Nov: first figure 67.24% (1,50,84,014 of 2,24,32,460 voters; ETV Bharat), then a final district-wise figure of 70.72%, highest Visakhapatnam 82.51%, lowest Alluri Sitharama Raju 62.01% (Telugu360, https://www.telugu360.com/andhra-pradesh-records-70-72-turnout-in-mptc-zptc-elections-visakhapatnam-tops-at-82-51/; M9 News). On 6 Nov five cyclone-hit mandals (Gopalapuram in East Godavari; Velerupadu, Buttayagudem, Jeelugumilli and Polavaram in the Eluru area) voted for 5 ZPTC and 60 MPTC seats, and repolls were held at seven booths in five districts; no turnout figure for 6 Nov at this update. Mandal parishad president and zilla parishad chairperson elections follow on 11 and 12 Nov. YSRCP alleged booth capturing and obstruction of voters in places including Dhulipalla and Pulivendula. Counting from 8 am on Saturday 7 Nov. Figures from The Hans India, 8 Nov 2026, 12:38 am; State Election Commission final figures not yet read. Final results read on Daijiworld (November 8, 2026, 10:55 pm); its MPTC rows sum to 7,749 against the stated 7,768, so 19 seats are unaccounted for. Percentages are our arithmetic on contested seats.

rows.name: Rajya Sabha bypoll, Madhya Pradesh
rows.result: Hardeep Singh Puri (BJP) declared elected unopposed on 5 November after the 3 pm withdrawal deadline passed with no rival left; the 12 November poll was not needed.
rows.notes: Seat vacated by L. Murugan, who resigned from the Rajya Sabha and the Union Council of Ministers on 14 Oct 2026; term_end is the end of his term, which the winner serves out. Schedule (ECI, announced 22 Oct): notification 26 Oct, last date for nominations 2 Nov, scrutiny 3 Nov, withdrawal by 5 Nov, poll 12 Nov (9 am to 4 pm) if contested, counting from 5 pm the same day, process to be completed by 16 Nov. BJP named Union Petroleum Minister Hardeep Singh Puri as its candidate on 28 Oct (Outlook, https://www.outlookindia.com/national/after-up-omission-bjp-fields-hardeep-puri-for-madhya-pradesh-rajya-sabha-seat). Outlook gave 16 Nov as the counting date; ETV Bharat's account of the ECI schedule says counting is on 12 Nov and 16 Nov is the completion date. Puri filed his nomination papers at the State Assembly building in Bhopal on 31 Oct, accompanied by Chief Minister Mohan Yadav and BJP state president Hemant Khandelwal; police detained Congress leaders ahead of planned protests against his candidature (The Pioneer, https://dailypioneer.com/india/hardeep-puri-files-nomination-for-mp-rajya-sabha-bypoll-congress-leaders-detained-ahead-of-protests). No other nomination was reported in sources read; whether he is elected unopposed will be known after withdrawals close on 5 Nov. Congress fielded independent Raj Kumar Lohani against Puri; he filed his papers before the returning officer in Bhopal on 2 Nov (Deccan Chronicle, https://www.deccanchronicle.com/amp/nation/congress-fields-independent-candidate-for-rs-by-election-in-mp-against-puri-2001243), so a poll on 12 Nov is likely unless he withdrew by the 5 Nov deadline; outcome of scrutiny and withdrawals not confirmed at this update. Update 6 Nov 2026: at scrutiny on 3 Nov the papers of Congress-backed independent Rajkumar Lohani were rejected because the Form 26 affidavit was missing at the deadline, and a second independent, Kante Sayanna, was rejected for lack of MLA proposers. The returning officer dismissed objections to Puri's affidavit. Congress MLAs Hemant Katare and Atif Aqeel were reported to plan a challenge in the Madhya Pradesh High Court (ANI; Open, https://openthemagazine.com/politics/hardeep-singh-puri-elected-unopposed-to-rajya-sabha-from-madhya-pradesh). date set to the day of the declaration.

rows.name: Manipur Legislative Assembly general election
rows.notes: ETV Bharat (5 Sep 2026) said the term ends 'by May 2027'. 13 March fits members taking oath on 14 March 2022 (Deccan Herald). No schedule announced.

rows.name: Goa Legislative Assembly general election
rows.notes: BOOM's tracker gives an approximate term end of about 14 February 2027 (polling date plus five years). Conflict unresolved; ECI Terms of Houses page could not be opened. Update 3 Nov 2026: a Bombay High Court (Goa bench) interim stay of late October on notifying Goa's ST population estimates has put the proposed reservation of four assembly seats for Scheduled Tribes before the 2027 polls in doubt; the state said it would file an SLP in the Supreme Court by 4 Nov (ThePrint/PTI, https://theprint.in/india/goa-to-move-supreme-court-against-hc-order-stalling-st-seat-reservation-process/3089079/).

rows.name: Punjab Legislative Assembly general election
rows.notes: Seat count per ThePrint (7 Aug 2026). No schedule announced. On 3 Nov 2026 the Supreme Court deferred Jagtar Singh Hawara's jail-transfer plea until after the polls, after an Intelligence Bureau report said the move would have a 'huge impact on the upcoming state elections'; PTI reported the polls are due early next year (ThePrint/PTI, https://theprint.in/india/transferring-beant-singh-murder-convict-to-punjab-will-have-huge-impact-on-elections-ib-tells-sc/3089068/).

rows.name: Uttarakhand Legislative Assembly general election
rows.notes: No schedule announced. Seat count per BOOM (BJP 47 of 70).

rows.name: Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly general election
rows.notes: Reports (News24; Economic Times via aggregator) expect UP to vote with the other four states, possibly in more than one phase. No schedule announced. Seat count per BOOM (BJP 255 of 403).

rows.name: Presidential election
rows.source_publisher: DT Next (headline and URL date only)
rows.notes: President Droupadi Murmu took oath on 25 July 2022, so her five-year term ends in July 2027. Exact term-end date not stated in any source read; no schedule announced.

rows.name: Himachal Pradesh Legislative Assembly general election
rows.notes: First session of the 14th Vidhan Sabha began on 22 December 2022 (The Tribune, https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/himachal/himachal-assembly-session-from-december-22-governor-issues-notification-461680), so under Article 172 the term runs into December 2027. Exact expiry date not confirmed from ECI; left null. Seat count per BOOM (INC 40 of 68).

rows.name: Gujarat Legislative Assembly general election
rows.notes: Newly elected MLAs took oath on 19 December 2022 (Deccan Herald, https://www.deccanherald.com/india/newly-elected-mlas-of-gujarat-assembly-to-take-oath-on-december-19-1172911.html), so the term runs into December 2027. Exact expiry date not confirmed from ECI; left null.

rows.name: Rajasthan panchayat elections (panchayat samiti and zila parishad members, sarpanch and ward panch)
rows.result: Phases 1 to 3 held on October 23, October 29 and November 4. The fourth and last phase is on November 14; counting of zila parishad and panchayat samiti members is on November 20 at district headquarters.
rows.source_publisher: ETV Bharat, citing State Election Commissioner Rajeshwar Singh
rows.notes: Announced by the State Election Commission on October 3, 2026. Covers 14,403 gram panchayats, 457 panchayat samitis and 41 zila parishads. Polling hours 7 am to 6 pm. Baran, Sri Ganganagar, Karauli and Kota districts vote after December 22, 2026. Nikhil Dey has questioned the voter rolls used (see our report of November 8, 2026); the commission says it used the pre-SIR roll of January 1, 2025. Phase 1 to 3 results not read.

rows.name: Kolkata Municipal Corporation election
rows.source_publisher: LiveLaw, reporting the Calcutta High Court order of November 6, 2026
rows.notes: No date. On November 6, 2026, a Calcutta High Court vacation bench barred the West Bengal State Election Commission from notifying the election until a challenge to the September 11 notification raising wards from 144 to 209 is decided by a single judge. The council has been dissolved since June 8, 2026.

excluded_unverified: Rajya Sabha biennial elections in 2027: states and dates not found in any reputable source.
Assembly or Lok Sabha bypolls in 2027: none announced as of 11 October 2026.
Early Punjab assembly poll in November 2026 (suggested by Arvind Kejriwal in June 2026; no ECI action).
Municipal polls with no announced dates (Bengaluru, Chandigarh and others).
